condition: Post-operative acute kidney injury (KDIGO stage 2) with nephrotoxic drugs
summary: 74-year-old man with CKD 3a on ramipril, day 2 after open right hemicolectomy on regular diclofenac: urine output 0.3 mL/kg/h for 14 h, creatinine 118 → 246, K 5.8, BP 102/60.

inputs.chiefComplaint: Low urine output after bowel operation
inputs.hpi: Day 2 after open right hemicolectomy for caecal cancer. Urine output 0.3 mL/kg/h for the last 14 hours via catheter (flushed, draining). Charted diclofenac 50 mg three times daily and ramipril continued; morphine PCA. Thirsty, drinking little. Baseline creatinine 118 µmol/L.

exam.general: Dry mucous membranes, cool peripheries. HR 98, BP 102/60 (usual 145/85), RR 18, SpO2 96% on air, T 37.2°C.
exam.abdomen: Midline wound clean. Soft, appropriately tender. Catheter draining concentrated urine.

labs.name: Urine dipstick
labs.resultText: SG 1.030, protein trace, blood negative, leucocytes negative, nitrite negative

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Acute kidney injury KDIGO stage 2 — day 2 after right hemicolectomy (hypovolaemia + NSAID + ACE inhibitor)
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: AKI stage 2 on CKD 3a: creatinine 246 from 118, oliguria 14 h. Pre-renal and nephrotoxic (diclofenac, ramipril). Stop diclofenac and ramipril, fluid assessment and challenge, K⁺ 5.8 monitoring, review enoxaparin dose, exclude sepsis/leak.

mustInclude.note: Urine dipstick for every AKI. Graded as management because the web prompt delivers it as a plan line.

K⁺ 5.8 is mild hyperkalaemia (UKKA 2020: insulin-glucose from 6.0 mmol/L); treat the cause and recheck.

mustExclude.proposedFix: Grade the hyperkalaemia prompt by UKKA 2020 bands: mild 5.5–5.9 → treat the cause and recheck; moderate/severe → insulin-glucose (±calcium with ECG changes).

guideline.name: KDIGO clinical practice guideline — acute kidney injury
guideline.section: Stage 2: creatinine 2.0–2.9 × baseline or urine output <0.5 mL/kg/h for ≥12 h; discontinue nephrotoxic agents where possible; assess volume status
guideline.citation: Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes AKI Work Group. Kidney Int Suppl. 2012;2:1–138.

guideline.name: NICE NG148 — Acute kidney injury: prevention, detection and management
guideline.section: Urine dipstick for all with AKI; consider stopping/withholding nephrotoxic drugs (NSAIDs, ACE inhibitors, ARBs, diuretics); ultrasound within 24 h when obstruction is suspected; monitor potassium; refer to nephrology by criteria
guideline.citation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. Acute kidney injury (NG148). London: NICE; 2019.

guideline.name: UK Kidney Association — clinical practice guideline: treatment of acute hyperkalaemia in adults
guideline.section: Mild 5.5–5.9, moderate 6.0–6.4, severe ≥6.5 mmol/L; insulin-glucose for K⁺ ≥6.0 mmol/L; ECG; treat the cause; dialysis for refractory hyperkalaemia or in dialysis patients
guideline.citation: UK Kidney Association. Treatment of acute hyperkalaemia in adults. 2020 (updated 2023).

rationale: Base post-operative AKI: pre-renal plus nephrotoxic drugs on CKD. Tests the AKI flag, stopping NSAIDs/ACE inhibitor, potassium, urinalysis, volume assessment and proportionate hyperkalaemia treatment.
